issues.description: In the template dd.py, UniqueTable.__init__ is defined to require a 'size' parameter, but later in the same file the global unique table is instantiated with UT = UniqueTable() (no argument). The solution implementation defines UniqueTable.__init__ with no parameters and instantiates UT = UniqueTable() accordingly. This mismatch in constructor signature in the template will cause a TypeError at import time and prevents students from running or working with the provided dd.py, despite the problem statement stating that dd.py already provides the basic functionality and should not need modification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the UniqueTable constructor signature in the template consistent with its usage. Either (A) remove the 'size' parameter so UniqueTable.__init__(self) performs default initialization (as in the solution), or (B) instantiate UT with an explicit size argument (e.g., UT = UniqueTable(some_size)). Prefer option A to match the solution and the problem statement assertion that dd.py already provides working functionality.
